question: What if I raise the price of Chips to 350?
headline: If the price of Chips goes from KES 300 to KES 350, about 8.2% fewer plates would sell and profit would rise by about KES 1,899 a month. You would keep 74.3% of each plate's price, up from 70%. Worth trying.

rows.label: Plates sold
rows.note: a rise in price is expected to sell fewer; a cut, more

rows.label: Profit a month
rows.note: more if positive, less if negative

rows.label: How sure
rows.note: from 66 plates sold in the last 30 days

assumptions.text: For every 10% on the price, about 5% fewer plates sell (your price sensitivity, adjusted for how fast Chips sells now).
The starting point is 2.2 plates a day, from the last 30 days of sales.
How guests react is a rough guide, not something measured; try a small change first.
